issues.failure_explanation: Theorem thm:spectre-limit controls, for each fixed mode i, the limit of rho(I^T(i)) as N -> infinity. The convergence factor of the full Schwarz iteration is governed by the supremum over the infinitely many TE/TM/TEM modes at finite N, so a rate independent of the number of subdomains requires a bound uniform in both i and N (or an inequality such as rho(I^T_N(i)) <= max(|a_i|+|b_i|) plus a uniform bound on the latter). Neither the theorem nor any argument in the source provides this: the inference from a pointwise-in-mode limit to a uniform convergence rate is a quantifier exchange, and it is exactly in the near-nilpotent regime, acknowledged just before the proposition, that the convergence of rho(I^T_N(i)) to its limit is not uniform in the parameters.

failure_location.quote: Finally, let us mention that this time, the limit spectrum is less than one (in modulus) which shows that the iterative Schwarz algorithm will converge with a rate independent of the number of domains and hence we have weak scalability.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either prove a bound uniform in the mode index and in N (for instance rho(I^T_N(i)) <= |a_i^T| + |b_i^T| together with sup_i (|a_i^T|+|b_i^T|) < 1 obtained from continuity in r and decay for large r), or weaken the conclusion to the per-mode statement and drop the claim of a convergence rate independent of the number of subdomains.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's headline conclusion - convergence with a rate independent of the number of subdomains, i.e. weak scalability of the full algorithm - and the corresponding abstract claim are not established by the formal content; only per-mode asymptotic stability is proved.
issues.title: Weak scalability concluded from a pointwise-in-mode limiting spectrum
issues.why_classification: A contained uniformity argument (or a limited weakening to per-mode conclusions) suffices; no new global proof architecture is needed and a recognizably comparable result survives, but the advertised weak-scalability guarantee is exactly what is at stake, so the issue exceeds a minor local fix.
